text: Go ahead.
>> The assembly will hear an address by his
excellency
E J Mong, the president of the Republic
of Korea. I request protocol to escort
his excellency and invite him to address
the assembly.
I would like to begin by expressing my
gratitude and respect to all member
states of the United Nations and the
staff of the UN Secretariat for their
dedication to a prosperous future for
all of humanity.
I extend my sincere congratulations to
his excellency Dr. Dr. Khalil Rahman on
assuming the presidency of the 81st
session of the UN General Assembly. I
also express my gratitude and pay
tribute to Secretary General Antonio
Gutares for his tireless service over
the past decade. Mr. President, Mr.
Secretary General, and distinguished
delegates. The United Nations, which has
a history of upholding human dignity and
pioneering the way for future
generations, now stands at a grave
crossroads.
The glacial flooding in Nepal that
claimed many lives and destroyed the
foundations of people's livelihoods
evidences that the climate crisis is a
reality of today, not tomorrow.
Persistent armed conflicts around the
world, including those in Ukraine and
the Middle East, continue to threaten
the survival of humanity. Emerging
technologies such as drones are rapidly
transforming warfare and posing serious
challenges to human rights and the
international law-based order.
Tensions surrounding the Strait of
Hormuz are undermining the fundamental
principles of free and safe navigation
and heightening the vulnerability of
energy supply chains.
Quote, "The United Nations was not
created in order to bring us to heaven,
but in order to save us from hell." End
of quote. These words of the second
secretary general of the UN, Doug
Hemershot, compel us to ask ourselves,
"Is the United Nations today capable of
saving humanity from war, poverty, and
disaster?
Is the United Nations living up to its
promise of restoring peace and achieving
sustainable development?
Ironically, the geopolitical crisis
brought on by the turbulence in
international order has reminded us of
the cherished value of multilateral
cooperation and international norms.
In an era of fragmentation marked by
fierce competition for immediate
survival, values of such as cooperation,
mutual prosperity and solidarity can
sound like hollow outcries. However,
like the founders who having witnessed
the ravages of war conceived the United
Nations, the deeper the crisis, the more
we need to return to the basic
principles of the UN.
Last year, I proudly announced from this
podium that the Republic of Korea, which
will be a beacon of life for global
citizens, has returned to the
international community.
Today, I stand here to make clear the
Republic of Korea's bold resolve to lead
the effort to restore the spirit of the
United Nations and reconnect the world
as a nation that has risen through the
solidarity of the international
community.
The worldwide popularity of K culture
serves as an example demonstrating that
universal empathy is possible,
showcasing the potential of global
connection.
The stories and content that grew out of
Korea's unique experience have become a
language of solidarity that crosses
borders.
Just as culture has connected people
across borders, so too can nations
reunite in the face of common problems.
The Republic of Korea will build on the
power of empathy and solidarity that
culture has brought to light. We will
harness that power to address the common
challenges facing all of humanity. To
that end, allow me to set out the three
visions of the K initiative toward
fulfilling this commitment. First,
the global AI universal basic society.
The artificial intelligence revolution
is both a massive opportunity and a
crisis for humanity. While it can be a
core driver of new prosperity and
sustainable development, it can it will
only deepen inequality and imbalance
unless we are properly prepared for it.
Younger people around the world in
particular are facing growing anxiety
about their employment and their future
as the pace of change becomes
increasingly difficult to keep up with.
This boils down to a clear direction for
the new era we seek to build. It is the
AI universal basic society where
everyone can benefit from technological
progress.
The Republic of Korea is pursuing an AI
transformation that will ensure stronger
protection of human fundamental rights
across fields such as social security,
labor, housing, and culture. Beginning
with our AI universal basic health
program
and I believe this resonates with the
core principle of the UN development
sustainable development goals which
prioritizes the guiding principle of
leaving no one behind. It also harnesses
the AI revolution as a new driver to
accelerate the realization of economic,
social, and cultural rights. The
Republic of Korea will build the global
AI hub platform to share this vision
with the international community in
collaboration with international
organizations, multilateral development
banks, the business sector, and
academia.
The Republic of Korea envisions a global
AI universal basic society where no
country or individual is left out from
access to the basic benefits of AI
development.
We will take the lead in shaping AI into
a tool for solving the shared challenges
we face such as the climate crisis,
public health, food insecurity and
refugee issues.
Second, the green transformation.
The climate crisis is often referred to
as a global group project shared by all
8 billion people on Earth. A single
country cannot tackle this challenge
alone. At the same time, abandoning both
cannot bring everyone on board.
The Republic of Korea announced its 2030
nationally determined contributions as
part of its active participation in the
Paris Agreement and UN- centered climate
action.
The Korea green transformation strategy
aims to convert our industrial structure
creating a virtual cycle in which carbon
neutrality leads to new growth engines
and decent jobs.
We are ready to share our experience and
best practices with the international
community.
Co-hosting the fourth UN Ocean
Conference with Chile in 2028 reflects
our commitment to leading discussions on
the sustainable development of our
oceans.
Third, the Coalition for Global Energy
Supply Chains.
Recently, there have been repeated
blockades of sea routes in the straight
of Hormuz and the Red Sea. This has
underscored the stark reality that the
weaponization of key energy and
logistics supply routes can send severe
shwack waves to the lives of ordinary
people around the world. Freedom of
navigation and safe passage through
international streets is a right
grounded in international law and serves
as a bedrock of the global economy.
Attacks on merchant vessels and threats
to the lives and safety of crew members
cannot be justified under any
circumstances.
While making greater use of existing
frameworks such as the International
Energy Agency, the Republic of Korea
will build a more robust framework of
cooperation for energy supply chains to
prevent the supply chain crisis from
escalating into a broader threat to the
global economy and people's livelihoods.
By nature, these problems cannot be
resolved by any one of us alone. At the
same time, we cannot afford to sit sit
idly by and wait for all nations to
arrive at a single solution. The most
urgent and realistic path is for
countries with the capacity and
willingness to supply global public
goods to join hands and broaden the
scope of cooperation.
I would like to call this a partnership
of constructive contributors.
I am not seeking to propose a new
organization nor an exclusive grouping.
The idea is to respect the functions of
the existing international order and the
UN work together in a flexible and open
manner in areas where each country has
particular strength and expand our ties
of cooperation into new areas.
By continuing to build on the
achievements of collaborating separately
yet together, we can move beyond
geopolitical rivalry, deadlock, and
fragmentation and rebuild trust in
multilateralism.
The United Nations must evolve with the
times.
Agreements reached at the negotiating
table must translate into real change on
the ground so that people around the
world can feel their impact in their
daily lives. We must reduce duplication
across organizations and programs,
accelerate decision making and direct
limited resources where they are needed
most.
In this spirit, the Republic of Korea
supports the UN80 initiative, which will
improve efficiency, prioritize field
operations, and deliver greater results.
We also support the reform of the UN
Security Council so that it operates in
a more effective domest democratic and
accountable manner.
The Republic of Korea will live up to
its responsibility and position to
deliver results that can be vividly felt
by people around the world across the
UN's three pillars of peace,
development, and human rights.
Through the Busan Global Partnership
Forum, we will continue to support
inclusive growth, share Korea's
development experiences such as the
Seang Unong, and continue to make
sustainable and innovative investments.
Mr. President, Mr. Secretary General,
and distinguished delegates,
when it comes to peace on the Korean
Peninsula, the Republic of Korea knows
firsthand the change that the United
Nations has brought about.
35 years ago, the two Koreas were
admitted to the UN as members on this
very stage.
It was a crucial turning point that laid
the foundation for peaceful coexistence,
freeing us from the relentless rivalry
and confrontation that followed our
division.
One year ago, I stated from this stage
that the Republic of Korea would begin a
new journey toward peaceful coexistence
and shared growth on the Korean
Peninsula.
Today, as we set out on this new
journey,
I would like to present to the
international community the three
blueprints for the road to peaceful
coexistence on the Korean Peninsula.
First is inclusive peaceful coexistence
built on mutual respect. Based on the
respect for each other's systems and
acknowledgment of our differences, we
will explore ways for shared growth
through cooperation.
We will continue to respect the north on
the international stage and seek
cooperation wherever possible.
We hope that opportunities will emerge
for us to work together in the
international community in areas such as
public health, disaster response, and
the climate crisis. Second, a stable
peaceful coexistence that renders
conflict unnecessary. We will work to
institute mechanisms for preventing
crisis and managing conflicts.
Reestablishing basic channels of
communication and building trust will be
the first step toward a stable peaceful
coexistence.
Third is responsible peaceful
coexistence contributing to world peace.
We will go beyond building a Korean
peninsula free from war and nuclear
weapons to promoting stability and
cooperation in Northeast Asia while
actively contributing to global efforts
to build a world free from war and
conflict. The most critical task is to
bring an end to this decades old war on
the Korean peninsula and establish a
lasting peace regime. For decades, the
two Koreas along with key countries such
as the US and China have recognized the
need for a peace regime on the Korean
Peninsula and discussed ways to achieve
it.
Fortunately, President Trump's resolve
has recently created a hard one
opportunity for change.
I hope the long suspended dialogue
between North Korea and the US can
resume without delay. We will lay the
groundwork for this to develop into a
dialogue among the parties aimed at
ending the war on the Korean peninsula
and transitioning to a peace regime. I
am confident that the dialogue for
establishing a peace regime on the
Korean peninsula can provide a valuable
framework not only for normalizing
relations among the parties concerned
but also for fostering shared growth
through multilateral cooperation and
promoting stability and cooperation in
Northeast Asia.
In this process, we will begin with a
stop to further advances in North
Korea's nuclear and missile
capabilities, followed by their
reductions in the medium term, moving
toward the Korean Peninsula free from
nuclear weapons over the long term.
I hope that the United Nations, which
created a pivotal moment for peaceful
coexistence on the Korean Peninsula 35
years ago, and the Security Council,
which has safeguarded the peace and
stability of the international
community, will once again play a
responsible and constructive role.
As a direct party to peace on the Korean
Peninsula and as a pacemaker, my
government will exert every effort to
open and sustain the path toward
dialogue.
Mr. President, Mr. Secretary General and
distinguished delegates,
the true performance of UN does not lie
solely in the figures and charts of the
reports or in the declarations made in
conference rooms.
The resonance of UN will be proven only
when children's laughter replaces
gunfire. When young people can enjoy the
opportunity to learn, work and take on
new challenges. and when anyone every
anywhere can choose to live the life
they want.
In 2015, the international community
adopted the sustainable development
goals as our shared commitments for a
bright future.
As we approach the 2030 deadline, now is
the time to sh chart a new path forward
for the next generation. It is
imperative for young people, our future
generation to define problems together,
formulate solutions and become
co-designers who can lead the action. We
need to bring more youth voices into
international decision making by
widening opportunities for participation
and communication as well as making bold
investments in the potential of the next
generation. The Republic of Korea can
testify more vividly than anyone else to
the noble power of solidarity embodied
by the United Nations. Our own
experience of achieving
industrialization and democratization in
the wake of war stands as proof of how
the world can bring about miraculous
changes with one mind and one heart of
the international community.
We are ready to repay that solidarity
with greater responsibility and
contribution. We will reconnect the
divided world, build a future that
leaves no one behind, and chart a course
for the next generation to dream of a
better tomorrow.
The Republic of Korea stands ready to
lead the way toward a peaceful
coexistence on the Korean Peninsula and
toward a United Nations that delivers
for all of us.
Thank you for your attention.
>> On behalf of the assembly, I wish thank
the president of the Republic of Korea.
